topicName: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Post-Incident Reviews
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Post-Incident Reviews in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Post-Incident Reviews are critical practices in software quality assurance. When a defect slips through manual testing and reaches production, it represents a process breakdown. Performing an RCA helps QA teams identify the underlying cause of the failure, prevent recurrence, and continuously improve manual test planning and execution."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"The 5 Whys Technique for Manual Testers"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 5 Whys is a simple yet powerful iterative interrogation technique used to explore the cause-and-effect relationships underlying a particular problem. By repeatedly asking the question "Why", the manual testing team can drill down from the symptom to the root cause."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Problem: A critical checkout button was disabled for all users in production."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Why 1: Why was the button disabled? Because a CSS style flag was incorrectly toggled by a recent frontend merge."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Why 2: Why was it toggled incorrectly? Because the code change altered a shared component layout."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Why 3: Why wasn't this caught in manual testing? Because the test case only verified the happy path without validating different user permission states."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Why 4: Why didn't the test case cover this state? Because the requirements documentation lacked clarity regarding conditional button states."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Why 5: Why was the requirement unclear? Because requirements were not reviewed by the QA lead prior to sprint development. (Root Cause)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Structuring a Post-Incident Review Report"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"After a production defect is resolved, the manual testing team should collaborate with developers and product managers to document the incident. Below is a standard template for a Post-Incident Review document."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"Incident Report Summary:
- Incident ID: INC-1042
- Date: 2023-10-25
- Impact: High (Checkout failure for all mobile users)
- Detection Source: Customer Support Tickets

Timeline of Events:
- 14:00 - Deployment to production completed.
- 14:15 - First user report of frozen checkout screen.
- 14:30 - QA team verifies production issue manually.
- 15:00 - Hotfix deployed and verified by QA.

Root Cause:
Lack of exploratory testing on mobile viewports for newly integrated payment gateway components.

Action Items:
1. Update manual test checklist to include mandatory mobile viewport verification.
2. Incorporate exploratory testing sessions before final sign-off."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Integrating RCA Learnings into Manual Test Cycles"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"An RCA is only as good as the preventive actions that follow it. Manual testers must translate findings into actionable improvements to ensure the same bug never occurs twice."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Update Test Suites: Add regression test cases covering the specific scenario that was missed."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhance Boundary Value Analysis: Ensure test scenarios explicitly test edge cases, permission levels, and environment-specific behaviors."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Refine Acceptance Criteria: Collaborate with product owners during refinement to ensure testability criteria are clear and unambiguous."}]
